pictures.scene: Rembrandt van Rijn, The Preaching of Saint John the Baptist — a lone preacher in a pale robe standing on a low rise with one arm flung wide over a great seated crowd in a wooded clearing, listeners perched in the branches above him and children sprawled in the dust at the front, after jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he went on from there to teach and preach in their cities, meanwhile john heard in prison about the works of christ, and he sent his disciples
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_preaching_of_john

pictures.scene: Duccio di Buoninsegna, Christ and the Samaritan Woman — Christ seated on the rim of a hexagonal stone well in a deep blue mantle, one hand raised in answer to a woman who stands facing Him with a clay jar balanced on her veiled head and her own hand lifted in question, to ask him, are you the one who was to come, or should we look for someone else, jesus replied, go back and report to john what you hear and see
pictures.name: pd_duccio_christ_and_the_samaritan_woman

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Healing the Blind — a close press of bearded elders and one smooth-faced youth gathered on the steps of a pillared courtyard, the foremost man stretching his arm straight out to point away down the stair while a figure in rose and gold turns aside before him, the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor, blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of me
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_healing_the_blind

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, The Marsh — a still brown woodland pool fringed with tall reeds and floating lily pads under leaning half-dead oaks, two white swans resting at the near bank and one small traveller barely visible in the shade beyond, as john's disciples were leaving, jesus began to speak to the crowds about john, what did you go out into the wilderness to see, a reed swaying in the wind, otherwise, what did you go out to see, a man dressed in fine clothes, look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings' palaces
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_marsh

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a preacher in a brown robe standing bareheaded in a dim forest clearing with both hands open as a dense ring of villagers in hats and white headcloths presses close to hear him, a few of them climbing into the trees for a better view, what then did you go out to see, a prophet, yes, i tell you, and more than a prophet, this is the one about whom it is written, behold, i will send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Adriaen Brouwer, Peasants Fighting — a wild-eyed man in a blue cap hauled backwards by a woman in a white headcloth who grips the arm holding his long knife, a second man bellowing over his shoulder and earthenware jugs standing on the bench behind them, truly i tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than john the baptist, yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he, from the days of john the baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it
pictures.name: pd_brouwer_fighting_peasants

pictures.scene: Washington Allston, Elijah in the Desert — a barren brown valley under a wide clouded sky with one great dead tree splitting the frame, a black raven perched on its bough and another swooping down toward the small grey-robed prophet who crouches alone among the stones, for all the prophets and the law prophesied until john, and if you are willing to accept it, he is the elijah who was to come
pictures.name: pd_allston_elijah_in_the_desert

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Children's Games — a wide town square swarming with children at dozens of games at once, rolling hoops and a barrel, riding on each other's backs, tumbling in a heap off a red railing and spinning tops in the dust before the tall pale houses, he who has ears, let him hear, to what can i compare this generation, they are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_kinderen

pictures.scene: Judith Leyster, Boy Playing the Flute — a boy in a soft red cap and a white ruff tipping his head back as he blows across a wooden flute, his eyes turned up and away, a violin and bow hanging on the bare grey wall at his shoulder, we played the flute for you, and you did not dance, we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn, for john came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, he has a demon
pictures.name: pd_leyster_fluitspeler

pictures.scene: Dieric Bouts, Christ in the House of Simon — Christ seated at a white-draped table set with loaves and a fish, raising His hand in blessing beside a frowning host in a jewelled blue cap, while a woman in green and blue kneels on the tiled floor and dries His feet with her loose hair, the son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners, but wisdom is vindicated by her actions, then jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of his miracles had been performed, because they did not repent
pictures.name: pd_bouts_christ_in_the_house_of_simon

pictures.scene: Rembrandt van Rijn, Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem — an old prophet in a fur-lined cloak slumped against a rock with his head propped on one hand and a heavy book at his elbow, gold and silver vessels heaped beside him and the burning city small and dim over his shoulder, woe to you, chorazin, woe to you, bethsaida, for if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in tyre and sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes, but i tell you, it will be more bearable for tyre and sidon on the day of judgment than for you
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jeremiah_lamenting_the_destruction_of_jerusalem

pictures.scene: John Martin, The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — a vast sheet of fire pouring down out of a red sky over a shattered city of dark walls and toppling towers while one small white-robed figure hurries away along the ridge in the foreground, and you, capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven, no, you will be brought down to hades, for if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in sodom, it would have remained to this day, but i tell you that it will be more bearable for sodom on the day of judgment than for you
pictures.name: pd_martin_the_destruction_of_sodom_and_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Rembrandt van Rijn, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — a white-bearded old man propped on a deep red bed laying his hand on the fair head of a small boy while the boy's father gently tries to shift it across, a second child watching from the bedside and a woman in dark velvet standing quietly by, at that time jesus declared, i praise you, father, lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children, yes, father, for this was well-pleasing in your sight
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_children_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Christ Giving His Blessing — a close half-length Christ against a dark ground, long brown hair falling past His shoulders and faint golden rays about His head, looking straight out at the viewer and raising two fingers of His right hand in blessing, all things have been entrusted to me by my father, no one knows the son except the father, and no one knows the father except the son and those to whom the son chooses to reveal him, come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and i will give you rest
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_giving_his_blessing

pictures.scene: Rosa Bonheur, Ploughing in the Nivernais — a team of broad cream and red oxen yoked two by two and straining through heavy turned earth, a young driver in a blue smock and a wide straw hat walking at their heads with a long goad raised over them, take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for i am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls, for my yoke is easy and my burden is light
pictures.name: pd_bonheur_ploughing_in_the_nivernais

lines.text: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.
Meanwhile John heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent his disciples
to ask Him, Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?
Jesus replied, Go back and report to John what you hear and see:
The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.
As John's disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings' palaces.
What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.
Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it.
For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.
He who has ears, let him hear.
To what can I compare this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others:
We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He has a demon!
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners! But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.
Then Jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.
At that time Jesus declared, I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.
